title: Review article: A systematic review and future prospects of flood vulnerability indices
journal: Natural Hazards and Earth System Sciences
study_objective: Systematically review flood vulnerability index construction methods and gaps.
variables_used: 95 peer-reviewed articles from 2002-2019.
weighting_or_modelling_method: Review of normalization, weighting and aggregation methods.
claimed_use_of_ranking: Decision support and hotspot identification.
validation_method: Systematic review; validation of index results discussed as independent secondary observable outcomes/proxies
same_period_or_future_validation: Mostly static or same-period in reviewed literature.
simple_baseline_comparison: Not identified as common in review screen
satellite_validation: Some reviewed validation used flooded-area maps.
sensitivity_analysis: Reports sensitivity analysis in 9.5 percent and uncertainty in 3.2 percent of reviewed studies
main_results: Only 11.6% validated results; 90.5% lacked sensitivity analysis; 96.8% lacked uncertainty analysis; temporal dynamics often disregarded.
main_limitations: Review scope through 2019 and vulnerability-index focus.
relevance_to_our_study: Strong evidence that validation, uncertainty and temporal dynamics are gaps.
notes: Figures from abstract/full text verified via NHESS/DOAJ. Full-text overlap screen: full text accessible. Review reports validation in 13.7%, sensitivity in 9.5%, uncertainty in 3.2%, and temporal dynamics gap; supports novelty of temporal/external validation but not broad validation-gap claim.
